answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can bid for work, then slash that stake when an independent audit proves fraud, such as claiming payment for duplicated outputs. Splitting one operator across a summit of aliases does not multiply its locked capital: each identity needs its own stake, while shared funds risk being slashed together. The atlas of public commitments makes audits verifiable; the ocean of possible aliases becomes costly to cross because every new identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture.
